clue.text: First aid received by blokes

indicators.note: something received by others is taken in and held within them

parts.note: blokes are men, in British slang
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some men are being given first aid after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First aid' reads as one phrase, but 'First' is split off as the definition: a maiden voyage or maiden speech is the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, maiden describes an initial attempt, like a ship's inaugural voyage or a politician's debut speech.

clue.text: Opera CD (arias) mum ordered

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters being put into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother has bought a compact disc of operatic arias.
explanation.definitionFit: Music drama is Wagner's term for his through-composed operas, and more widely any opera treated as unified drama.

clue.text: Childhood home, elaborately and ornately decorated

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
fancy describes something elaborate and ornate

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the ornate, richly decorated house they grew up in.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the earliest stage of a person's life, so it stands for childhood in general.

clue.text: Additional bit-part player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more than is usual or expected
second meaning: a film actor hired for a crowd scene

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like one description of a minor actor, but 'Additional' is a separate adjective meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means surplus as an adjective, and as a noun a performer with a tiny non-speaking role in a film.

clue.text: Wound inhibiting head of campaign abroad demonstrating armoured vehicle

indicators.note: inhibiting means holding back, here pictured as holding something in

parts.note: a scar is the mark of a healed wound
someone abroad is out of the country

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of campaign

explanation.surface: A campaign leader abroad has been wounded, which shows how dangerous the trip was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like a verb about injury to the leader; it is a noun for the outer piece. 'Abroad' here simply means out.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout car is a light military vehicle with armour, used for reconnaissance ahead of the main force.

clue.text: Chicanery involving revised rental for system installed in the home?

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked into a new form
involving means taking something in as part of itself

parts.note: chicanery is trickery or deception
the word rental rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord's trickery over an altered rent agreement is a regular scam in homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition that is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Central heating is a system of boiler, pipes and radiators fitted throughout a house to warm it.

clue.text: Unscrupulous lunatic? He changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters do not stay as they are

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man has become dishonest or simply mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person without moral principles, willing to act dishonestly or wrongly.

clue.text: A site of many battles seen from pilot's place?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pit for cockfights, and so any region fought over repeatedly, as Belgium was called the one of Europe
second meaning: the compartment from which an aircraft is flown

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pilot viewing battlefields from the air; the two parts are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an arena for fighting birds, extended to frequent battlegrounds, and the flight deck of an aeroplane.

clue.text: Pass turn

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to rotate over and over

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a board-game instruction to skip a go; each word is separately a meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to roll on or roll by as it passes, and a rolling ball keeps turning over.

clue.text: Developing Hispanic areas covering miles in Chile, Peru etc.

indicators.note: developing implies growing into a different shape
covering means lying around something, so the rearranged letters surround the extra one

parts.note: these two words rearranged
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Spanish-speaking regions in South America are growing over many miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile and Peru are examples of the former Spanish colonies in the Americas where Spanish is spoken.

clue.text: Fastener from piece of equipment, sort mostly carried by tennis star

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the following name

parts.note: Marat Safin, the Russian former world number one

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
a piece is just a small part, here the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of equipment
a sort is a type

explanation.surface: A tennis player carries a clip taken from part of their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Marat Safin is a Russian former world number one, winner of the US and Australian Opens; 'sort mostly' loses one end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is a bent pin with a covered point, used to fasten cloth or nappies.

clue.text: Former church leader's beginning to surpass all others

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of leader

explanation.surface: A retired church leader begins to outshine everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former church leader' looks like one ex-bishop; it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstanding, doing better than everyone else at something.

clue.text: Vessel damaged pier stanchion

indicators.note: something damaged has been knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship has struck and damaged a supporting post of the pier.
explanation.definitionFit: A container ship is a large cargo vessel built to carry goods packed in standard steel boxes.

clue.text: Live over a period of time under canvas? That shows improvement

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: under canvas means camping, so the next part is put inside a tent

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
a term is a fixed period, such as a school term

explanation.surface: Spending a while camping in a tent proves good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts BE on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment is the act of making something better, so it is a synonym for improvement.

clue.text: Excellent bet backing on run out

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, from end to start

parts.note: to lay a bet is to place it

explanation.surface: A gambler places a superb bet on a batsman being run out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is run out when the stumps are hit before they complete a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal can mean splendid or first-rate, as in a royal welcome or a right royal feast.

clue.text: One reprimanded after 50 let loose

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the first-named part is placed second

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
berated means scolded angrily

explanation.surface: A person was told off after fifty people were set free.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals supply both numbers here, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean set free from confinement or control, as a prisoner released from captivity.

clue.text: Join the most important couple and take a stimulating drink

parts.note: to splice is to join ropes or film
taken as written
main means chief or most important
a brace is a pair, as of pheasants

explanation.surface: A newly married star couple celebrate with a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is old Royal Navy slang for issuing an extra rum ration, now meaning to have a celebratory drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval idiom originally meant serving sailors an extra tot of rum, and now means having alcohol to celebrate.

clue.text: See 16
Be left at home with that girl, Italian

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
her refers to a girl
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Someone is left at home with an Italian girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be left' looks like abandoned; it means to receive something in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property when someone dies, which is what being left something in a will means.

clue.text: I'm driven through illuminated border

indicators.note: driven through means pushed into the middle of the next word

parts.note: lit means lighted up
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A driver passes along a brightly lit boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or edge, the line beyond which something does not extend.

clue.text: Crazy about North American pop star

parts.note: mad means crazy
on means about, as in a book on birds
NA is the abbreviation for North American

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about an American pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is the American singer who has been one of the world's best-selling pop stars since the 1980s.

clue.text: Sharpest drive upset spinner in the field, one with long legs?

definitions.text: spinner in the field, one with long legs?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket spinner fielding is upset by a very hard shot, though he has long legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner in the field' suggests a cricket bowler; here a spinner is a creature that spins webs or silk, found in fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest spider, or harvestman, is a long-legged arachnid common in fields at harvest time; daddy-long-legs is another name.

clue.text: Quietly press for pogrom

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Someone quietly pushes for an organised massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is the violent removal of unwanted people from a group, close in meaning to an organised massacre.

clue.text: Portray pig eating bit of hay

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, here the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of hay

explanation.surface: A painter depicts a pig munching some hay.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to depict or represent it, as a painting portrays its subject.

clue.text: World Cup hero injured netting second

indicators.note: netting means catching inside a net, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: hurt means injured
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A football hero, hurt, still scores a second goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Netting' suggests scoring a goal; it means catching. Geoff Hurst scored a hat-trick for England in the 1966 World Cup final.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurst is famous as England's hat-trick scorer when they won the football World Cup in 1966.

clue.text: Lack of education in church is stifling good girl

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the other parts are held inside

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England
G is the abbreviation for good
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A church is silencing a well-behaved girl who never went to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In church' looks like a location; the word in is itself part of the outer letters, split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge, which is what having had no education leaves you with.

clue.text: Drop out being shy? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means not the whole word, so its end is cut

parts.note: withdrawn means reserved and shy

explanation.surface: Someone shy is considering quitting a course, though not wholly.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw from a race or course is to pull out of it, the same as dropping out.

clue.text: Leave SW river holding record

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within its grasp

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, in south-west England
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A river in the south-west carries a record downstream as it leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away from a place, which is what leaving means.
